description: A fang hung on a leather cord, worn smooth by a thumb. Somebody believed in it right up to the end.
lore: The shine is on the left face of the base, where a right thumb sits when it is not thinking about it, and that is years of somebody. [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]] has learned to ask about the charm before she asks the name. You wake in the grass wearing what you wore, and for the first hour most people cannot produce their own name to save themselves — but a man who cannot tell you what he is called will tell you straight off that he won this from his sister's husband, that it is a boar's, that it is not a boar's and he has always known it. Then the rest comes up the rope behind it. A good share of the names on that meadow were fetched out by a piece of tooth on a string, and she has never once said so to the person it worked on.
gm_notes: Solveig's actual technique at a waking, stated plainly for the first time: the object first, the name second. Any newly woken NPC can be given one worn possession and a story about it, and that is the handle a player uses to get them talking.
